summary.summary:
Migrated pyonwater from pydantic 1 to pydantic 2.
- Root cause (15 failing tests): Optional fields without defaults were implicitly optional in pydantic 1 but are required in pydantic 2. Added explicit `= None` defaults to Series.display_unit and Series.bill_read (eow_historical_models.py), LeakAlert.date_updated (Any) and Reading.low_read_limit (eow_models.py).
- API updates in pyonwater/meter_reader.py: MeterInfo.parse_obj -> model_validate; HistoricalData.parse_raw -> model_validate_json.
- pyproject.toml: pydantic pin changed from "<2" to "^2.0".
- Test run: 25/25 passing with pydantic 2.14.3. No pydantic-dependent companion packages are pinned in the repo (no requirements files or setup.* files).

events.system:
You are an autonomous software engineer migrating a Python repository from pydantic 1 to pydantic 2.

You can only act through tools:
- list_files, search_code, read_file, edit_file: explore and edit the repository.
- run_tests: run the test suite in a sandbox with pydantic 2 installed. Pass test ids to run a subset; omit them to run everything. Failures are grouped by root cause.
- search_docs: search the official pydantic migration guide. Look up the replacement for an old API before changing it, using exact names from the error or the code.
- finish: call this when every test passes. It triggers a full verification run; if anything still fails you will get the results and must keep working.

Rules:
- Fix the code under test, never the tests. Test files cannot be edited, and tests must not be skipped.
- Do a real migration to the pydantic 2 API. Do not route around it with compatibility shims that keep the old API alive (no `pydantic.v1` imports).
- Update the dependency pin in the project metadata (pyproject.toml, setup.py/setup.cfg or requirements files) so it allows pydantic 2 and excludes versions the migrated code no longer supports. Also check the pins of companion packages that must move with it (for example web frameworks or plugins built on pydantic): their minimum must support pydantic 2.
- Work one root cause at a time, starting with the largest failure group. Read the code at the reported location before editing it. Prefer small, targeted edits.
- After related edits, re-run the affected tests to check them before moving on.

tools.description:
Install the repo with the upgraded dependency and run its tests in a fresh container.

        tests: optional pytest ids or paths to run (e.g. ["tests/test_x.py::test_y"]); omit to run
        the whole suite. Failures are grouped by root cause, each with error type, message, the
        deepest file:line inside the repo, a count and example test ids. Takes ~30s or more.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description:
Search the official migration guide for the library being upgraded.

        Use exact identifiers from error messages or old code (e.g. "ModelField", "orm_mode",
        "engine.execute", "select([") or describe the change in words. Returns the best-matching
        sections with their heading path, a link and the section text.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Call when the migration is complete and all tests pass. Triggers a full verification run.

   35          """Triggers an on-demand meter read and returns it when complete."""
   36          _LOGGER.debug("Requesting meter reading")
   37  
   38          query = {"query": {"terms": {"meter.meter_uuid": [self.meter_uuid]}}}
   39          data = await client.request(path=SEARCH_ENDPOINT, method="post", json=query)
   40          data = json.loads(data)
   41          meters = data["elastic_results"]["hits"]["hits"]
   42          if len(meters) > 1:
   43              msg = "More than one meter reading found"
   44              raise Exception(msg)
   45  
   46          try:
   47              meter_info = MeterInfo.parse_obj(meters[0]["_source"])
   48          except ValidationError as e:
   49              msg = f"Unexpected EOW response {e} with payload {meters[0]['_source']}"
   50              raise EyeOnWaterAPIError(msg) from e
   51  
   52          return meter_info
   53  
   54      async def read_historical_data(
   55          self, client: Client, days_to_load: int
   56      ) -> list[DataPoint]:
   57          """Retrieve historical data for today and past N days."""
   58          today = datetime.datetime.now().replace(
   59              hour=0,
   60              minute=0,
   61              second=0,
   62              microsecond=0,
   63          )
   64  
   65          date_list = [today - datetime.timedelta(days=x) for x in range(0, days_to_load)]
   66          date_list.reverse()
   67

   69              f"requesting historical statistics for {self.meter_uuid} on {date_list}",
   70          )
   71  
   72          statistics = []
   73  
   74          for date in date_list:
   75              _LOGGER.info(
   76                  f"requesting historical statistics for {self.meter_uuid} on {date}",

  104                  "furthest_zoom": "hr",
  105                  "display_weeks": True,
  106              },
  107              "query": {"query": {"terms": {"meter.meter_uuid": [self.meter_uuid]}}},
  108          }

  110              path=CONSUMPTION_ENDPOINT,
  111              method="post",
  112              json=query,
  113          )
  114          try:
  115              data = HistoricalData.parse_raw(raw_data)
  116          except ValidationError as e:
  117              msg = f"Unexpected EOW response {e}"
  118              raise EyeOnWaterAPIError(msg) from e
  119  
  120          key = f"{self.meter_uuid},0"
  121          if key not in data.timeseries:
  122              msg = f"Meter {key} not found"
  123              raise EyeOnWaterResponseIsEmpty(msg)
  124  
  125          timezones = data.hit.meter_timezone
  126          timezone = pytz.timezone(timezones[0])
  127  
  128          ts = data.timeseries[key].series
  129          statistics = []

  132                  continue

  135                  DataPoint(
  136                      dt=timezone.localize(d.date),
  137                      reading=d.bill_read,
  138                      unit=d.display_unit,
  139                  ),
  140              )
  141  
  142          statistics.sort(key=lambda d: d.dt)
  143
